problem: Consider the section of the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4$ that lies in the second quadrant. Given that $x=x(t),$ $y=y(t),$  and that $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=\sqrt{3}$ on the circle at the point where $x=-\sqrt{3},$ find the value of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}$ at that point.

feedback.problem: Consider the section of the hyperbola $\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}=1$ that lies in the second quadrant. Given that $x=x(t),$ $y=y(t),$ and that $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=4$ on the hyperbola at the point where $x=-3,$ find the value of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}$ at that point.
feedback.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{3})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{3})-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (\frac{2x}{3})-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot y & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=4$ and $x=-3.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}4\cdot (-2)-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot y & =0 \\ -8-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot y & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We also want to substitute for $y,$ but we are not given this value. However, we can find it by substituting $x=-3$ into the equation of the hyperbola.

At the point where $x=-3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{(-3)^{2}}{3}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ 3-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & =1 \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & =2 \\ {y}^{2} & =4 \\ y & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used $y>0$ since we're only interested in the second quadrant.

 Finally, substituting $y=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-8-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot 2 & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$
